title: DNS Systems: Resolution & Records
description: Welcome to the DNS Core Lab. DNS is the 'phonebook' of the network. When it fails, users see 'No Internet' even if the wires are perfect. You will handle 12 realistic scenarios focusing on internal resolution, record management, and cloud integration.
reportOverview: This report documents your ability to identify DNS zone issues, record typos, cache symptoms, and propagation delays.

intro.objective: To navigate the DNS hierarchy and master the tools (nslookup, dig, ipconfig) used to verify how names are translated into IP addresses.
intro.scenario: You are the primary admin for 'Nexus Corp'. The company uses a hybrid environment with on-prem Active Directory and several cloud-based SaaS tools. Your task is to resolve resolution breaks in the ticket queue.
workflow_tips: Use 'nslookup' to see exactly which server is answering; if it's 8.8.8.8, you might be bypassing internal records.
Check the 'FQDN' (Fully Qualified Domain Name). A missing dot or a typo in the suffix is a common cause of failure.
Flush the DNS cache (ipconfig /flushdns) after applying a fix to see immediate results.

tickets.title: The 'Invisible' Domain Controller
tickets.summary: A technician is trying to join a new server to the domain 'corp.nexus.com', but it keeps saying 'Domain not found', even though they can ping the DC's IP address.

triage.q: Why can the client ping the DC but fail to join the domain?
options: The client is using a public DNS server that doesn't know internal zones

diagnosis.q: What record type does Windows look for to find a Domain Controller?

debrief.summary: Internal AD resources require internal DNS for SRV records.
debrief.takeaway: Never use public DNS as primary on AD-joined machines.

tickets.title: The 'Wait 48 Hours' Myth
tickets.summary: Marketing updated the IP for the blog 4 hours ago. Some customers see the new site, but the Director still sees the old one.

triage.q: Why is the Director still seeing the old site?
options: ISP cache still has the old record due to high TTL

diagnosis.q: What does a TTL of 86400 tell a DNS server?
options: Keep record in cache for 24 hours

fix.q: What should have been done before migration?

debrief.takeaway: Lower TTLs 24+ hours before a planned move.

tickets.title: Emails Bouncing: SPF Fail
tickets.summary: A partner rejects emails from your CEO, claiming they are 'Unauthorized'.

triage.q: Why is the mail being rejected?

diagnosis.q: What does an SPF record do?

triage.q: If IP works but name doesn't, where is the failure?

tickets.title: The 'Internet is Down' (Except it's not)
tickets.summary: Primary DNS crashed. Secondary is up, but half the office is offline.

diagnosis.q: How do Windows clients handle DNS lists?
options: Try first, if timeout, try second
Update DHCP to include both 10.0.0.1 and 10.0.0.2

tickets.title: The Alias Ambiguity
tickets.summary: You moved the wiki to SharePoint. You want 'wiki/' to go to 'sharepoint.nexus.internal'.

triage.q: What record type allows one name to point to another?

diagnosis.q: Why use CNAME instead of A record?
options: If SharePoint IP changes, wiki record stays valid

tickets.title: Shadow IT Discovery
tickets.summary: Security sees traffic to a mystery server. You have the name, you need the IP.

triage.q: Finding IP from Name is what lookup?

diagnosis.q: Security wants to find other names for that IP. Where to look?

fix.q: What record maps IP back to Name?

options: Servers only check syntax, not logic

tickets.title: Microsoft 365 Verification Failure
tickets.summary: M365 setup can't find the verification record.

triage.q: What record is Microsoft looking for?

tickets.title: The 'Sticky' Mistake
tickets.summary: You fixed a wrong IP in DNS, but your laptop still hits the old one.

diagnosis.q: Why hasn't laptop checked server again?
Default next step for unknown records?
